summary: The Runway SAFE-T Act requires the Federal Aviation Administration to establish a task force focused on improving airport driver training and modernizing safety practices in airport movement areas. It also amends federal law to allow grant funding for airports to purchase movement area safety technology and technology-enabled training systems for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

affected_groups.effect: Will participate in the task force and become eligible to apply for and receive federal grants for vehicle movement area technologies and training systems from fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
Will be represented on the task force and may experience updated, more consistent training programs and new situational awareness technologies in airport movement areas.
affected_groups.group: Airport ground vehicle operators and air traffic personnel

affected_groups.effect: The FAA Administrator must convene the task force, receive its final report, and oversee the administration of the new grant program for airport vehicle safety projects.

key_provisions: Establishes a task force on airport driver training programs no later than 6 months after enactment.
Directs the task force to include diverse aviation representatives, ranging from airport executives and labor workers to FAA designees and NTSB observers.
Requires the task force to develop recommendations to improve training consistency, recurrent training requirements, and safety technologies while addressing cost and workforce barriers.
Requires the task force to submit a final report to the FAA Administrator and specific congressional committees within one year of its establishment.
Authorizes the Secretary to provide grants to airport sponsors for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to purchase vehicle movement area technology and training systems.

Establishes priority rules for grant distribution, favoring projects designed to reduce surface safety incidents, improve situational awareness, adapt to airfield geometry, or address financial and workforce barriers.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or dollar limits authorized for the grant program.
Whether compliance with the task force's future recommendations will become mandatory for all commercial service airports.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Runway SAFE-T Act requires the Federal Aviation Administration to establish a task force focused on improving airport driver training and modernizing safety practices in airport movement areas. It also amends federal law to allow grant funding for airports to purchase movement area safety technology and technology-enabled training systems for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a formal, multi-stakeholder mechanism to review and recommend nationwide safety improvements for drivers operating vehicles on airport runways and taxiways. Furthermore, by creating a specific grant funding stream for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, it provides direct federal financial support for commercial service airports to acquire modern safety hardware, software, and technology-enabled training systems.

title: Runway SAFE-T Act
